title: A GUI input queued on gui_lock across a human handback runs with no burst, so its changes get no snapshot and no gui_changes record for up to 600 s
description: _call_tool decides whether a GUI input needs a new burst before it acquires gui_lock. While a human holds the desktop a lease exists, so needs_snapshot returns False and the input is queued on gui_lock instead of opening a burst. If the human hands the desktop back inside that gap, the queued input runs with no open burst: it writes files as uid 1001, marks its input time, and from then on needs_snapshot returns False for every later input until the interval expires, so no snapshot, no burst and no gui_changes row are produced. The agent can therefore make a series of unrecorded desktop changes whose only recovery point predates the human takeover.
root_cause: The burst decision is taken outside the lock that serializes execution: service.py:343 evaluates _needs_snapshot (gui_bursts.py:52-63, False while a lease is present) before _run_tool acquires gui_lock at service.py:136, and the re-check under the lock (_check_control, service.py:152-161) validates only the lease and the pending-takeover marker, never burst presence. _handback_locked (service.py:528-543) releases the lease and calls forget_input inside that lock, so the queued input resumes into a state where its earlier decision premise is gone, and mark_input (service.py:139) then suppresses the next burst decision.
intended_behavior: Every GUI input that executes must be covered by an open burst bound to a snapshot taken before that input, and each burst must close into a gui_changes record. A decision taken before waiting on a lock must be re-validated after the lock is acquired.

trace.description: Agent token; GUI tools are approval-free by design and run as uid 1001 in the desktop session.
_needs_snapshot is evaluated here, before any lock; with a takeover lease present it returns False (gui_bursts.py:58).
The GUI branch acquires gui_lock without a timeout, so the queued input can wait arbitrarily long.
After acquiring the lock it re-checks the lease and the pending marker only; burst presence is not part of the check.
The human handback releases the lease and calls forget_input while holding gui_lock, exactly in the gap.
The resumed input executes and calls bursts.mark_input regardless of whether a burst is open.
The fresh input time makes the next decision False, so no burst or baseline is taken for up to gui_snapshot_interval.
No burst exists to close, so no gui_changes row is written for these changes.

evidence.description: Burst decision taken before the lock.
gui_lock acquired afterwards without a timeout.
needs_snapshot returns False while a lease exists, which is why the queued input skipped the burst.
mark_input fresh timestamp suppresses the following burst decision.
Handback releases the lease and forget_input inside the lock-held section.

conditions.description: A sandbox agent token; GUI tools are approval-free by design.
The agent GUI call must already be waiting on gui_lock when the human handback runs; keeping several GUI calls cycling widens the window, and audit-lock contention widens it further.
A snapshot newer than gui_snapshot_idle exists, so needs_snapshot would otherwise be False.

execution.attacker_perspective: An agent that wants to change the desktop without leaving a gui_changes record keeps GUI calls in flight while a human is in control, then acts immediately after the handback.
payloads: POST /sandboxes/sb_x/tools/click {args:{x:10,y:10}} x4 while a takeover lease is held
takeover and handback by the human
instructions: Bounded local harness in the approved audit sandbox: real AgentBox, GuiBursts and DesktopControl with a fake sandbox/audit and deterministic scheduling.

Seed one click so a burst and snapshot exist; take the desktop with a lease; queue a click on gui_lock; run _handback_locked(); then issue further clicks and read bursts state, snapshot count and audit rows.
execution.observed_result: 5 clicks created 5 files but exactly one gui_changes row (snap_1/human_takeover/created_1); needs_snapshot stayed False and the snapshot count stayed 1; the queued click and the following three returned 200 executed. The control run with an open burst logged gui_changes for the same change.

remediation.strategy: Re-evaluate needs_snapshot after acquiring gui_lock in _run_tool, fail closed when no burst is open, and key needs_snapshot on burst presence rather than only on input timestamps. Regression test: hold the lease and the lock with an input queued, release the lease, release the lock, and assert the input is refused or opens a burst and never marks input without a burst.

likelihood.reason: Needs a handback inside the window while an agent GUI call is queued; keeping several GUI calls in flight makes the collision repeatable but not certain.

impact.reason: Desktop changes made through the agent GUI tools become unrecorded and unrecoverable past the last snapshot, defeating the burst-level audit and recovery guarantee the N-1 mitigation rests on.

confidence.reason: Deterministic reproduction on the real AgentBox, GuiBursts and DesktopControl objects; only the sandbox and audit were faked, and the control run shows the same path records changes when a burst is open.
